On load, `AuthLoader` in `src/app/provider.tsx` wraps the whole app and calls `useUser` from `src/lib/auth.tsx`. That calls `getUser`, which sends `GET /auth/me` through the shared Axios instance in `src/lib/api-client.ts`. While that request is pending, `AuthLoader` shows a full-screen spinner. Once it settles, the result is cached in React Query. `ProtectedRoute` in `src/lib/auth.tsx` wraps the `/app` routes in `src/app/router.tsx`. If `user.data` is missing, it redirects to `/auth/login?redirectTo=<current path>`. The login and register routes and `auth-layout.tsx` read `redirectTo` and send the user there after sign-in.

When any request gets a 401, the response interceptor in `src/lib/api-client.ts` does two things. It shows an error toast with the server's message through `useNotifications`, and then it sets `window.location.href` to the login path with `redirectTo` set to the current pathname. The request promise is still rejected afterwards. The interceptor does not distinguish `/auth/me` from other endpoints, so a signed-out visitor also gets the error toast and the hard redirect from the initial `/auth/me` call. I did not trace how `react-query-auth` handles that rejection, so I can't say which navigation wins in every case.

One detail in that interceptor looks wrong. It reads `redirectTo` from a new, empty `URLSearchParams()` instead of from the current URL, so it always falls back to `window.location.pathname`. The page the user wanted is still restored, but only its path, without any query string. Making it read `window.location.search` would fix that. I haven't changed anything.
